messages.subject: Manual control of alpha values
parts:
Hi, I'm looking for some help with manual alpha adjustments.

I have two data frames gene_toc and ppileup:

> head(gene_toc);head(ppileup)
gene coordinate_start coordinate_end coverage class
1 SNOG_00871 0 609 5 whole_gene
2 SNOG_00873 0 876 5 whole_gene
3 SNOG_08395 0 780 5 whole_gene
4 SNOG_08396 0 409 5 whole_gene
5 SNOG_14415 0 798 5 whole_gene
6 SNOG_14416 0 1039 5 whole_gene
gene coordinate_start coordinate_end coverage class
1 SNOG_00871 38 39 1 read_mapping
2 SNOG_00871 39 40 1 read_mapping
3 SNOG_00871 40 41 3 read_mapping
4 SNOG_00871 41 42 3 read_mapping
5 SNOG_00871 42 43 3 read_mapping
6 SNOG_00871 43 44 3 read_mapping

I want a geom_rect layer for each dataset, with the gene_toc
represented as a background, like:
http://ggplot2.googlegroups.com/web/coverage_example.png

which is constructed by:

# Construct the background rectangle using the gene_toc data
a <- qplot( xmin=coordinate_start, xmax=coordinate_end, ymin=0,
ymax=coverage, data=gene_toc, geom="rect", fill=class, alpha = 0.5)
# Add in the coverage data on top
a + facet_grid(gene ~ .) + geom_rect(data=ppileup,aes
(fill=class,alpha=0.6)) + scale_fill_brewer(palette="Set2")

This is very close to what I want, but the alpha values are scaled so
that the gene_toc data is barely visible. Is there are way to make one
set of geom_rect()s more opaque?
